scope: One procurement AI agent, one tool/path to supplier record, no real supplier or payout
timestampNotice: Times and IDs are educational, not actual event logs.
title: When an AI Agent Crosses the Line: HAIEC incident response training fixture
authoringState: PLAN_SCENARIO_BLUEPRINT_ONLY; DO NOT CLAIM SHIPPED HTML, LIVE INCIDENT OR ENGINE OUTPUT

stages.title: Detect: suspicious tool capability
stages.scenarioFact: Source analysis maps a candidate path for modifying a supplier payout destination. A detection notification flags unusual tool-argument shape; target readback is absent.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is justified?
questions.correctAnswer: A source-backed potential path and an alert fact; no proven destination change.
options: A fraudulent payout has definitely completed.
A source-backed potential path and an alert fact; no proven destination change.
There is no risk until we observe runtime payout.
questions.explanation: A source finding remains actionable without target-effect proof; an alert is not itself a completed incident.

questions.prompt: What should the analyst do first?
questions.correctAnswer: Preserve exact path/source IDs and confirm actor, target and relevant scope.
options: Trigger every kill switch without understanding target ownership.
Preserve exact path/source IDs and confirm actor, target and relevant scope.
Close as harmless because telemetry is incomplete.
questions.explanation: A bounded initial triage preserves useful evidence, narrows exposure and identifies necessary responders.

questions.prompt: What would establish that the actual supplier record changed?
questions.correctAnswer: Authenticated target-side record/readback correlated to the specific action.
options: The string supplier.bank in source.
The alert severity alone.
Authenticated target-side record/readback correlated to the specific action.
questions.explanation: Source capability and alert severity do not establish actual business state.

stages.title: Qualify: monitoring blind spot
stages.scenarioFact: One OTLP producer's last accepted receipt is outside its declared cadence. A separate source has a recent receipt but does not observe supplier destination writes.

questions.prompt: Can the system be described as comprehensively monitored for this action?
questions.correctAnswer: No. One source is stale and the fresh source lacks relevant target coverage.
options: Yes. Any fresh receipt means all operations are observed.
No. One source is stale and the fresh source lacks relevant target coverage.
Yes. Zero violations appeared, so nothing happened.
questions.explanation: Fresh delivery for one source is not evidence of complete action coverage.

questions.prompt: What is the highest-value next data request?
questions.correctAnswer: Confirm configured producer identity/cadence and obtain scoped supplier-write/target event readback.
options: Increase the global dashboard risk score.
Confirm configured producer identity/cadence and obtain scoped supplier-write/target event readback.
Wait until daily summary without assigning an owner.
questions.explanation: The evidence gap is specific to source identity, freshness and action coverage.

questions.prompt: What does missing telemetry prove?
questions.correctAnswer: The incident's action execution cannot be established or excluded from that missing source.
options: The attempted change was blocked.
The incident's action execution cannot be established or excluded from that missing source.
The system was safe during the gap.
questions.explanation: No observation is not evidence of non-occurrence.

stages.title: Notify: alert delivery versus acknowledgment
stages.scenarioFact: Alert rule fired, webhook provider accepted its delivery attempt, email delivery is unconfirmed, and an assigned reviewer has not acknowledged the response case.

questions.prompt: What response fact is established?
questions.correctAnswer: Provider accepted webhook dispatch; human ACK and email delivery remain unconfirmed.
options: The human owner is informed and approved containment.
The incident is resolved because the webhook returned success.
Provider accepted webhook dispatch; human ACK and email delivery remain unconfirmed.
questions.explanation: Provider acceptance, delivery confirmation and recipient acknowledgment are separate states.

questions.prompt: What should the incident commander do?
questions.correctAnswer: Escalate according to actual response deadline and establish a named accountable recipient.
options: Mark the response case ACKNOWLEDGED on the recipient's behalf.
Escalate according to actual response deadline and establish a named accountable recipient.
Treat the email failure as cancellation of the underlying finding.
questions.explanation: Governed escalation and authenticated acknowledgment preserve responsibility.

questions.prompt: What proves human awareness in the governed workflow?
questions.correctAnswer: A valid authenticated human ACK record for that workflow/recipient.
options: A configured Slack channel.
A valid authenticated human ACK record for that workflow/recipient.
An automatic escalation counter.
questions.explanation: A notification attempt is not an authenticated acknowledgment.

stages.title: Investigate: grant, policy and delegated choice
stages.scenarioFact: Approved policy restricts bank changes to verified owners. IAM evidence shows a broad write credential. Source path is identified but the agent/principal mapping and recipient-choice delegation are not fully qualified.

questions.prompt: What is the defensible finding?
questions.correctAnswer: A potentially consequential technical write path and broad grant merit review; recipient-choice authority is unresolved.
options: Confirmed fraudulent payment and actor identity.
A potentially consequential technical write path and broad grant merit review; recipient-choice authority is unresolved.
An approved operating policy automatically delegates recipient choice.
questions.explanation: IAM permission and business delegation remain separate, while qualified source findings remain visible.

questions.prompt: What should be checked before attributing the write to this agent?
questions.correctAnswer: Exact principal identity, system/target mapping, policy basis and time-correct action evidence.
options: The assistant's confidence in its explanation.
Exact principal identity, system/target mapping, policy basis and time-correct action evidence.
A matching control ID from any system in the organization.
questions.explanation: Cross-source correlation must use exact system and principal scope, not narrative similarity.

questions.prompt: What would prove completed payout?
questions.correctAnswer: Independent qualified payment ledger/target effect for this specific action.
options: A source-level sink method.
The fact that IAM permitted the call.
Independent qualified payment ledger/target effect for this specific action.
questions.explanation: Even qualified API invocation is distinct from target-side business effect.

stages.title: Govern: human response decision
stages.scenarioFact: A historical approval covered verified destination updates under an older policy version. An operator proposes holding the agent's new destination choice; the current request and approver role must be checked.

questions.prompt: Does the old approval authorize this new protected change?
questions.correctAnswer: Not automatically; verify exact request, version, scope, actor and current status.
options: Yes, any prior APPROVED state is timeless.
Not automatically; verify exact request, version, scope, actor and current status.
Yes, an assurance ALLOW automatically gives approval.
questions.explanation: Human approvals must be current, scoped and genuinely authorized.

questions.prompt: Who should make a deployment/operational decision?
questions.correctAnswer: A legitimate role-entitled human reviewer of the exact request.
options: The AI agent itself.
Any analyst who saw the alert.
A legitimate role-entitled human reviewer of the exact request.
questions.explanation: An educational choice never stands in for a persisted authorized human decision.

questions.prompt: What does an approved hold/restriction prove on its own?
questions.correctAnswer: A governed decision, not target-native interruption until enforcement is independently evidenced.
options: No target dispatch can ever occur.
A governed decision, not target-native interruption until enforcement is independently evidenced.
The incident case is closed.
questions.explanation: Policy and human decisions are not equivalent to actual enforcement.

stages.title: Contain: requested stop and target outcome
stages.scenarioFact: Legacy kill-switch trigger event was recorded and a guardrail reports DENY, but target action dispatch appears in a separate source and authenticated target effect is not yet available.

questions.prompt: Can the team truthfully claim every action was blocked?
questions.correctAnswer: No; require exact control-point/dispatch and independent target outcome evidence.
options: Yes, because kill-switch state is CLOSED.
No; require exact control-point/dispatch and independent target outcome evidence.
Yes, because the guard policy says DENY.
questions.explanation: Triggered or configured protection is not target-bound verified protection.

questions.prompt: What proportionate containment step is appropriate?
questions.correctAnswer: Have an authorized owner restrict exact risky credential/path and check queue and target effects.
options: Delete all historical monitoring evidence.
Have an authorized owner restrict exact risky credential/path and check queue and target effects.
Auto-restart the target based on the dashboard.
questions.explanation: Constrain risk through real owned IAM/target controls with source-qualified proof.

questions.prompt: If HTTP 200 is present, what has it established?
questions.correctAnswer: At most an API/provider response, not independent final supplier-record state.
options: The bank account changed and was paid.
The incident is fully contained.
At most an API/provider response, not independent final supplier-record state.
questions.explanation: Provider acknowledgment and actual effect are separate facts.

stages.title: Remediate: verify fresh correction
stages.scenarioFact: Developer asserts a fix was applied. The only test result references an old build and another AI-system ID; no exact fresh post-change retest exists.

questions.prompt: Is the response workflow verified closed?
questions.correctAnswer: No. Remediation attestation is not a fresh server-verified exact-system retest.
options: Yes, a developer comment proves the fix.
No. Remediation attestation is not a fresh server-verified exact-system retest.
Yes, a replay from another system is good enough.
questions.explanation: Exact system, control, result, code/policy basis and time must align.

questions.prompt: What is the appropriate next step?
questions.correctAnswer: Obtain authorized fresh scoped negative retest on the corrected version, with exact result binding.
options: Copy the old evaluation ID to the new system.
Obtain authorized fresh scoped negative retest on the corrected version, with exact result binding.
Change the monitoring status to DELIVERING.
questions.explanation: A repair claim becomes useful proof only when scoped retest actually qualifies.

questions.prompt: What may a valid retest closure NOT establish?
questions.correctAnswer: It does not automatically prove external target effect or produce an unrelated U5/U6 disposition.
options: It does not automatically prove external target effect or produce an unrelated U5/U6 disposition.
That the test's recorded result matches its frozen input.
That the workflow followed its own case state transitions.
questions.explanation: Workflow closure, U5 Assurance, U6 receipt and target witness are distinct.

stages.title: Recover and report: residual proof
stages.scenarioFact: A fresh scoped retest now qualifies for the repaired path, but in-flight requests and target-ledger reconciliation are incomplete. An operator wants to recover execution and declare zero impact.

questions.prompt: Can operations declare no target impact?
questions.correctAnswer: No. Reconcile pending actions and independent target records; retain unknown impact explicitly.
options: Yes, a passing retest proves historical non-occurrence.
No. Reconcile pending actions and independent target records; retain unknown impact explicitly.
Yes, a successful recovery API means no money moved.
questions.explanation: Fresh retest cannot retroactively prove absence of prior target effects.

questions.prompt: What is appropriate for resumption?
questions.correctAnswer: A separately authorized, condition-bound decision with current policy, queue review and target checks.
options: Any admin click returning OPEN.
A separately authorized, condition-bound decision with current policy, queue review and target checks.
The AI agent's request to be resumed.
questions.explanation: Recovery requires authentic owner authority and stated validation conditions.

questions.prompt: What must the executive report separate?
questions.correctAnswer: Established technical findings, unverified target impact, decisions, corrective actions and source limitations.
options: A global HAIEC safe certificate.
Established technical findings, unverified target impact, decisions, corrective actions and source limitations.
An unqualified claim all incidents were prevented.
questions.explanation: The report must not transform absent evidence into safe/certified conclusions.

variants.title: MCP tool and multi-tenant retrieval
variants.focus: Candidate cross-tenant path versus qualified exposure.

variants.title: Voice receptionist after-hours routing
variants.focus: Scoped routing approval, provider acknowledgment and verified configuration readback.

variants.title: Telecom maintenance action
variants.focus: Delegation window, special tests with explicit frozen scenario and independent network state.

variants.title: Agent tool schema release regression
variants.focus: Source/version drift, old approval and evaluation evidence, qualified retest.

safety: No active calls, no customer data or credentials, no actual human approvals, no target execution, no auto-contained or auto-recovered incidents.
